info.title: CEXY API
info.description:
REST API for a cryptocurrency exchange.

## Conventions

**Amounts are strings.** Every monetary value is a decimal string such as `"1.50000000"`,
never a JSON number. A JSON number is parsed into an IEEE-754 double by most clients,
which cannot represent `0.1` exactly — so a number would silently corrupt balances.
Parse them with a decimal library, not a float.

**Errors have machine-readable codes.** Every failure returns
`{"error": {"code", "message", "details", "request_id", "retryable"}}`. Branch on
`code`, never on `message`, which may change. `retryable` says whether an identical
retry could succeed.

**Two-factor is mandatory.** Registration cannot complete without enrolling an
authenticator, and a correct password alone never returns a session. Sensitive actions
additionally require a *recently* verified code — call
`POST /account/security/two-factor/verify` to refresh the window.

**Pagination.** Histories use opaque cursors: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. They
carry no `total`, because counting an ever-growing collection on every page is a full
scan and the number is stale before it renders. Catalogues use offsets and do include a
total.

**Idempotency.** The operations that move money out of an order book honour an
`Idempotency-Key` header, and declare it: `POST /wallet/withdrawals`,
`POST /account/transfers`, `POST /account/sub-accounts/{id}/transfer`,
`POST /futures/transfers`, `POST /futures/transfers/return`, and
joining and leaving a pool. A retry with the same key and body replays the original
response; the same key with a *different* body is rejected with `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT`.
Orders do not take the header: set `client_order_id`, which is unique per account, and look
an order up by it after a timeout. Cancelling is naturally safe to repeat.

**Rate limits.** Responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and
`X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the window resets. A request without credentials
counts against its IP address: 120 a minute. A signed-in session counts against its
account and an API key against the key: 600 a minute each. A `429` carries
`retry_after_seconds` in the error's `details`, and `Retry-After`.

**WebSocket.** `/api/v1/ws` carries every realtime channel on one connection. Every client
message with an `id` is answered with that `id`: `authenticated` (with `user_id`),
`subscribed`, `unsubscribed`, `pong`, or `error` with a `code` and `message`. Private
channels need an `auth` frame carrying a session access token first; API keys do not open
them. An `orderbook.update` carries the top 50 levels of both sides in full and replaces the
previous book.

tags.description: A TradingView UDF datafeed. Point the charting library at /api/v1/udf. Like the aggregator feeds, this follows TradingView's conventions rather than this API's: OHLCV arrives as parallel arrays of JSON numbers, and `s` is a status string rather than an HTTP code.

get.summary: Every pool and what it holds.

post.description: The pool's resting orders for the market are cancelled first, because reserves locked in an order cannot be paid out. Shares are burned and a proportional slice of both assets is returned.

400.description: More shares than the account holds

404.description: No pool, or no position in it

409.description: The idempotency key was reused with a different body

post.description:
Both assets are taken, in the ratio the pool already holds — only the quote that ratio requires is debited, however much is offered. The first join into an empty pool sets the price, and is refused if it strays far from the market's last traded price.

Send `Idempotency-Key` so a timed-out request can be retried without adding liquidity twice.

400.description: The amounts or the implied price were refused

409.description: The idempotency key was reused with a different body

get.summary: Server time, so a client can detect clock skew before it breaks two-factor.

post.description:
Funds are reserved before the order reaches the book, so a matched order can never be unfunded. On a buy the reservation covers the value plus the **taker** fee, which is the worst case — a maker fill releases the difference.

Set `client_order_id` to make a retry safe: it is unique per account, so a repeat is refused before any funds move, and `GET /trading/orders/by-client-id/{client_order_id}` recovers the outcome. `Idempotency-Key` is not honoured here.

200.description: Order accepted, with any immediate fills

409.description: That client order id is already in use

422.description: Insufficient funds, or the market is unavailable

503.description: The market is saturated; retry shortly

get.summary: One order, looked up by the id the client supplied.

404.description: No such order on this account

post.summary: Cancels every open order, and every stop order that has not triggered, optionally within
post.description:
one market.

Best-effort: a failure on one order does not stop the rest, and every outcome is reported. A panic-button endpoint that stops at the first problem is worse than useless. A stop waiting for its trigger (`pending_trigger`) is cancelled too and its reservation released, so nothing fires into the market after the call.

An order still being placed when the call starts (status `pending`, for as long as its own placement request runs) is waited for, up to 500 ms per call in total: cancelled if it opens, reported in `already_closed` if it fills or is refused, and in `failed` with code `INVALID_STATE` if it is still being placed at the deadline. Orders placed after the call starts are not part of it. At most 500 orders per call; `has_more` says there are others.

Limited to 30 calls a minute per account, on top of the general request limit.

429.description: Over 30 calls a minute for this account; `details.retry_after_seconds` says when to retry

AccountIdResponse.description: The id of the account a credential belongs to, and nothing else.

user_id.description: Account id: the same hex as the realtime `authenticated` reply's `user_id`.

Amount.description: Exact decimal amount, serialized as a string to avoid floating-point precision loss. Example: "1.50000000".

ApiKeyResponse.description: An existing key. Never carries the secret.

allowed_ips.description: Permitted source addresses. Empty means unrestricted.

id.description: Opaque key identifier, used to revoke it.

key_id.description: The public key id, sent as `X-API-Key`.

last_used_at.description: When it was last used, if ever.

ApiScope.description:
Scope attached to an API key.

 Scopes narrow what an API key may do. They apply to API keys only: a signed-in session carries none and is not limited by them.

AssetNetworkResponse.description: An asset's policy on one network.

contract_address.description: Contract address or chain asset id, for a token.

deposit_confirmations.description: Confirmations before a deposit is credited.

memo_label.description: What to call the memo field in a UI.

memo_supported.description: Whether the network uses a memo / destination tag.

token_kind.description: How the asset exists on this chain.

withdrawal_decimals.description: Decimal places a withdrawal amount is truncated to.

withdrawal_fee_asset.description: Asset the withdrawal fee is charged in.

decimals.description:
Accounting precision: the decimal places the exchange records internally.

Use this for arithmetic. For rendering, use `display_decimals`.

display_decimals.description:
Decimal places to show in a user interface.

Always less than or equal to `decimals`. Rounding for display is presentation only and must never be fed back into a request.

icon_key.description: Identifier for a client-bundled icon, when no logo URL is set.

logo_url.description: Logo URL, when the operator has configured one.

max_price_age_secs.description:
How old this asset's price may be before it is refused, in seconds.

The global default unless an operator set an override for this asset. Exposed beside the flag because the flag alone cannot explain itself: an asset that is not stale after a week and one that is not stale after an hour look identical without it.

networks.description: Networks this asset can be deposited to or withdrawn from.

notice.description: Operator note, e.g. why deposits are paused.

trading_enabled.description: Whether the asset may appear in markets.

usd_price_stale.description:
Whether that price is too old to compute with.

When true, the exchange refuses to derive anything from it: daily limits and auto-approval fail closed rather than guess, and a stored USD value is recorded as absent rather than as a confident wrong figure.

usd_price_updated_at.description:
When that price was last set.

Exposed because the price is typed in by an operator and refreshed by nothing — there is no feed. Without the timestamp a caller cannot tell a price set an hour ago from one set last month, and both look equally authoritative.

held_incoming.description: Internal transfers to this account still held, soonest released first; empty when none. Their sum is part of `locked`. Shows at most 100.

sequence.description: This balance's sequence: it rises with every change to it, and `balance.updated` carries the same number as `data.sequence`. Apply an event only if its sequence is greater than the one this snapshot holds. 0 for a balance never touched.

CancelAllRequest.description: Cancels every open order, optionally within one market.

symbol.description: Limit the cancellation to one market. Omitted or `null`, every market's open orders are cancelled.

CancelAllResponse.description:
What a bulk cancellation achieved.

Every order the call handled is in exactly one of `cancelled`, `already_closed` and `failed`.

already_closed.description: Orders that closed on their own (filled, rejected, cancelled elsewhere) before this call reached them. Nothing was done to them, and they are not failures.

failed.description: Orders that could not be cancelled in this call. Check `failures` for why, then refresh or call again.

failures.description: Why each order in `failed` could not be cancelled.

has_more.description: More open orders exist than one call handles (500). Call again.

CancelFailureResponse.description: Why one order could not be cancelled.

code.description: The error code of the attempt, as in any error response: e.g. `INVALID_STATE` for an order still being placed when the wait ran out, or `MARKET_UNAVAILABLE`.

deposit_confirmations.description: Confirmations before the deposit is credited.

memo.description: Memo / destination tag. **Required when present** — a deposit without it may be unrecoverable.

memo_label.description: What to call the memo field in a UI.

explorer_url.description: Explorer link, when the network has one configured.

note.description: Operator note, e.g. why it was reversed.

output_index.description: Position within the transaction. Distinguishes two outputs of one transaction.

DepositStatus.description: Lifecycle of an incoming blockchain deposit.

DetailValue.description: A structured value attached to an error. Kept deliberately narrow so that no accidental secret (a token, a key, a full document) can be attached.

ErrorBody.description: The `error` object as it appears on the wire.

fields.description:
Per-field validation messages, keyed by request field name.

Present only on validation failures. Render each message beside its input.

message.description: Human-readable description. May change between releases.

request_id.description: Correlates this response with server logs. Quote it in support requests.

retryable.description: Whether an identical retry could succeed.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable, machine-readable error identifiers.

Serialized as `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`. Adding a variant is backwards-compatible; renaming or removing one is a breaking API change.

ExchangeConfigResponse.description:
Public exchange configuration.

Everything a frontend needs to render itself without a deploy: branding, limits, supported intervals, and whether the exchange is in maintenance.

default_page_size.description: Default page size for paginated endpoints.

email_verification_required.description: Whether registration verifies the email address with an emailed code before the authenticator step. Lets a signup form show the right number of steps up front.

features.description:
Feature flags a frontend may use to hide unavailable functionality.

Presentation only. The backend enforces every rule independently.

maintenance_message.description: Message to show while in maintenance.

maintenance_mode.description: Whether the exchange is in maintenance mode.

two_factor_freshness_seconds.description: Seconds a verified two-factor code authorises sensitive actions for.

websocket_path.description: Where to open the realtime connection, relative to this API's origin.

websocket_protocol_version.description: The realtime protocol version this server speaks.

fee_asset.description: Asset the fee was charged in.

FuturesTransferId.description: Unique identifier of a futures collateral transfer.

HeldIncomingResponse.description: An internal transfer credited to `locked` and not yet available.

available_at.description: When it becomes available, unless an operator cancels it before then.

LedgerEntryResponse.description: One entry from the account's ledger.

sequence.description: Position in this account's history for this asset.

oneOf.description: A manual operator adjustment. Always accompanied by an audit event.
A liquidity pool join or exit.

A movement of collateral to or from a futures account.

Every entry a transfer produces carries the same one, so the reservation, the release and the completion can be read back as one event — which is what an operator resolving an ambiguous transfer needs.
A system-originated credit with no user counterparty (rebate, promotion).

LedgerReference.description: What caused a ledger entry: one kind of cause per variant, told apart by `type`.

LiquidityRole.description: Whether a fill added liquidity (maker) or removed it (taker).

MaintenanceReason.description: Machine-readable reasons a capability is unavailable.

MaintenanceState.description: Why a capability is currently unavailable.

message.description: Operator-supplied explanation, when there is one.

MarketResponse.description: A tradable market and its current ticker.

last_trade_at.description: Time of the most recent trade.

price_decimals.description: Decimal places a price may carry.

quantity_decimals.description: Decimal places a quantity may carry.

trading_starts_at.description: When trading opens, for a market not yet live.

average_block_seconds.description: Typical seconds between blocks, for estimating confirmation time.

deposits_operational.description:
Whether deposits on this network are actually being detected.

False means either half of the pipeline is down: the last scan pass failed — a refused block range, a rate limit, a node that answers but will not serve logs — or finality could not be established, so deposits are being held rather than credited.

Deposits sent now will be credited late, whenever the chain recovers, rather than lost. This is the field a status page should use to say deposits are degraded; `reachable` only says the node replies, which it may well do while yielding nothing.

explorer_address_url_template.description: Template for an address explorer link. `{address}` is substituted.

explorer_tx_url_template.description:
Template for a transaction explorer link. `{txid}` is substituted.

Absent when the operator has configured none; render no link rather than guessing a URL.

reachable.description:
Whether the node answers at all.

Narrower than it sounds, and deliberately so: a reachable node can still be failing to yield deposits. Do not render this alone as "network up".

NotificationKind.description:
What a notice is about.

A closed enum so a client can render each kind deliberately — an icon, a colour, a link — rather than pattern-matching on prose that may be reworded.

resource_id.description: The referenced resource's opaque id, for linking.

OrderBookResponse.description: One side of the order book, aggregated by price.

bids.description: Bids, best first, as `[price, quantity]` pairs.

sequence.description:
The realtime sequence this snapshot is current as of.

Each `orderbook.update` on the `orderbook:{symbol}` websocket channel carries both sides of the top 50 levels in full (`data.full` is always `true`) and replaces the previous state; there are no deltas to buffer. Ignore an update whose `sequence` is at or below the one you hold. A gap only means a book was missed: the next update replaces it whole.

client_order_id.description: Your identifier, if you supplied one.

closed_at.description: When it reached a terminal state.

fee_asset.description: Asset the fees were charged in.

status_reason.description: Why the order was rejected or cancelled.

triggered_at.description: When the trigger fired, if it has.

OrderSide.description: Which side of a market an order takes.

OrderType.description: Order types the matching engine accepts.

PasswordRules.description: Password constraints, published so a form can validate locally.

allows_email_substring.description: Whether the password may contain the account's email address.

description.description: A short description of any further rules, for display beside the input.

PlaceOrderRequest.description:
Places an order.

Set `client_order_id` to make a retry safe: it is unique per account, so a repeat is refused before any funds move, and `GET /trading/orders/by-client-id/{client_order_id}` recovers the outcome. `Idempotency-Key` is not honoured for orders.

client_order_id.description: Your own identifier. Unique per account.

PlaceOrderResponse.description: The result of placing an order, including anything it executed immediately.

fills.description: Fills produced on entry, oldest first.

PoolId.description: Unique identifier of a liquidity pool.

PoolResponse.description:
A pool as a client sees it.

Reserves are the custody account's balances, so they include liquidity currently locked in resting orders. `price` is the curve's mid, which sits between the pool's own best bid and ask by exactly its fee — it is not a traded price.

fee_percent.description: The pool's fee, in percent, priced into every quote it rests.

PoolStatus.description: Whether a pool quotes, and whether it accepts new liquidity.

PublicTradeResponse.description:
A public trade.

Deliberately anonymous: no account identifiers, and no indication of which side was the resting order beyond the aggressor direction.

ServerTimeResponse.description:
The server's clock.

Two-factor codes are time-based, so a client can compare its own clock against this before a skewed clock gets a correct code rejected.

epoch_ms.description: Current time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

iso.description: Current time as RFC 3339 with an explicit UTC offset.

SortDirection.description: Sort direction for a paginated listing.

can_withdraw.description: Always `false`. A sub-account has no withdrawal path — stated explicitly so a client does not have to infer it.

id.description: Opaque identifier. Use it to transfer funds and to issue API keys.

TimeInForce.description: How long an order remains eligible to match.

TriggerDirection.description:
Which way the price must move for a stop to fire.

Explicit rather than inferred from the side, because the inference is ambiguous: a sell stop below the market is a stop-loss, and a sell stop above it is a take-profit. Both are legitimate, and guessing wrong means an order that fires at exactly the wrong moment — which is the one thing a protective order must never do.

UserId.description: Unique identifier of a user account.

last_used_at.description: When it was last withdrawn to.

WithdrawalHistoryEntry.description: One transition in a withdrawal's life.

cancellable.description: Whether the account holder may still cancel it.

completed_at.description: When it confirmed to the required depth.

fee_asset.description: Asset the fee was charged in.

history.description: Transitions this withdrawal has been through.

WithdrawalStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an outgoing withdrawal.



`pending_approval` waits for an operator to approve the withdrawal. `broadcast_unknown`
means the transaction may have been sent: the funds stay debited until it is resolved
against the chain.

api_key.name: X-API-Key
api_key.description: Identifies the key. Sent with `X-API-Secret`, which authenticates it — both headers are required. Create one at `/account/api-keys`; the secret is shown once and never again. A key can read and trade. It can never withdraw or transfer, whatever its scopes, because those need a recently verified two-factor code and a program cannot produce one.

api_secret.name: X-API-Secret
api_secret.description: Authenticates the key identified by `X-API-Key`. Never sent in a query string: a URL reaches access logs, proxy logs and `Referer` headers.
